title: Allowed Amount at Issue on a Joining Late-Filed TRICARE Select Line — Appeals and Grievances Training Sheet
content:
Appeals and Grievances training sheet — the allowed amount at issue on the joining line, for a further TRICARE Select posting of a claim joining an open Claim Factual Reconsideration on that claim, both carrying the late-filing denial.

**Rule.** The allowed amount at issue on the joining line is set from the provider's own paid lines for the patient: where the provider has three or more paid TRICARE Select lines for the patient in the joining line's service class posted in the twelve months before the day the amount is figured, it is the average of their allowed amounts, rounded to the cent; where it has one or two such lines, it is the allowed amount of the provider's most recently posted paid line in that class for the patient; where it has none, it is the amount the provider billed on the joining line, which for a nonparticipating provider is first divided by one plus the tier's nonparticipating balance-billing limit so that nothing such a provider may bill above the allowed amount comes into dispute, rounded to the cent.

**Questions answered by the rule**

*Which lines are counted?* In figures: the look-back runs 12 months, and the average is used from 3 paid lines upward. The paid lines read are the patient's TRICARE Select claim lines with the line outcome paid, from the same provider and in the same service class as the joining line. The balance-billing limit is the nonparticipating balance-billing limit percentage of the TRICARE Select tier the line was billed under, taken as hundredths of one (a limit of p percent divides by one plus p hundredths); the division applies only where the provider is recorded on the joining line as non-network nonparticipating.

*When exactly is a line inside the twelve months?* A paid line counts as posted in the twelve months before the day the amount is figured when fewer than 12 whole months have passed from its posted date to that day: figured on 2026-10-11 (a hypothetical date), a line posted on 2025-10-12 counts, while a line posted on 2025-10-11 — 12 whole months earlier — does not.

*The provider has exactly 3 qualifying paid lines (hypothetical allowed amounts 120.00, 135.50 and 141.25). What is the allowed amount at issue?* The average: 396.75 divided by 3, which is 132.25.

*The provider has 2 qualifying paid lines, 118.00 posted first and 126.40 posted most recently (hypothetical).* The allowed amount of the most recently posted one, 126.40; 2 lines do not reach the 3 needed for an average.

*The provider has no qualifying paid line and is nonparticipating; it billed 460.00 on the line and the tier's limit is a hypothetical 15 percent.* 460.00 divided by 1.15, which is 400.00. Had the provider been participating, the billed 460.00 would stand.
